title: hotfix: SLO enforcement + circuit breaker thresholds causing excessive load shedding during regional failover
author: Aisha Patel
description: When triggering a regional failover we observed the SLO enforcement circuit breakers were tripping too aggressively for a subset of short-lived transient errors. This resulted in excessive load shedding and degraded customer experience in the failover window. This hotfix tightens the circuit-breaker trip logic, adds hysteresis and backoff windows, and adjusts the SLO enforcement throttle so that transient spikes during region handoffs do not cascade into full-service shedding. The changes are intentionally small and conservative: we prefer slightly higher latency during an ongoing failover over dropping requests. Changes include code fixes in the runtime circuit-breaker, routing logic to avoid double-counting errors across layers during failover, added integration and unit tests, and updated alerting thresholds to reduce noisy signals during a failover. Testing performed: unit tests, integration tests across simulated multi-region failover, and a staged canary deploy with manual failover exercises. Rollback plan: revert the single squash-merge commit and redeploy the previous main build; health-checks and canary will be used to validate the rollback. Checklist: 1) Reproduce locally and in staging (done) 2) Add unit & integration tests (done) 3) Update observability and runbook (done) 4) Canary deploy to staging then prod (done) 5) Monitor SLOs and alerts for 24h after merge (ongoing). Related: ENG-4212 (investigation), ENG-4230 (postmortem), incident SUP-914. No breaking API or config changes required for customers.

release_notes: Hotfix: reduce unnecessary load shedding during regional failovers by changing circuit-breaker trip logic, adding hysteresis/backoff windows, and tightening SLO enforcement to avoid double-counting errors across routing and runtime layers. Reduces customer-impacting request drops during failover. No API breaking changes.
